steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Enable administrator-level encryption.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Image number (0018_admin).

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Activating recorder... Beginning video record.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: While I slept, the ruins of our homeland nurtured new life.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Originium is what guides their development, reshaping the lifeforms from Talos-II to have a similar appearance to us.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I am rather fortunate. I have been able to leap across the millennia to communicate with them. I have even considered myself one of the people of this land for a time, experiencing their past and future.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But in the end, I am not of here. I have even begun to feel... uneasy about Theresa's efforts.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: If the Originium Project ends in failure, no, even if it is merely postponed for some time... Theresa, Kal'tsit, even the future that I promised to Amiya...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The inhabitants of this planet, some of the few lifeforms known to us, are but illusions that will break at the slightest touch.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I have been lying to them and to myself for a very long time now. But... how will I explain it to Kal'tsit? Or to Theresa, or Amiya?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Am I supposed to tell them that all the pain they have been through is the key to their salvation, and they must stop fighting?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: That all of Terran civilization is a fleeting dream, and only by being assimilated into Originium will we have the opportunity to avert our fate?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Seeing the lives of those they call the Infected dissipate like smoke brings pain to my heart.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It has long been a common sight on Terra, but it always marks the end of life—sorrowful and cruel.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It has been too long since I've heard a voice full of life. I can't just see them as unexpected sparks.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But what I see cannot be called a warrior's death.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Rather, they have given in to the Originium's assimilation, passing through death to join the Assimilated Universe, a chance where life can break through the deepest darkness.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Should I bow in silence at their deaths...? Or should I quietly rejoice at the smooth progression of the project?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It is for this reason that Theresa dedicates herself to her research. Kal'tsit, our AMa-10, has also chosen to believe in the potential of Terra, chosen to resist Originium and put an end to war...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But what about me?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The Originium Project was built upon the efforts of countless generations, and in that time, billions of our compatriots have died, all in exchange for a mere ten thousand years that I have spent waiting and waiting.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: And now, the flint and tinder are in my hands. After all the long years. How could I abandon it?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Because Terra has left me pleasantly surprised in a few short years? Because of the choices that Theresa and Kal'tsit made?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Even if Amiya has moved me to compassion, would I not have been the selfish one all along?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: They... awakened me to be their salvation, but in truth, I am destined to bring them to annihilation.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: They awakened me, their destroyer, as if I were their savior...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: (Chokes back tears)

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Amiya... Kal'tsit...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: What should I do?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Priestess... What should I do?

a.text: Perhaps I should reveal everything to Kal'tsit and Theresa.
Originium has led them down roughly the correct path. Arrogant though it may be, this has been sufficient for these souls to perform a new kind of miracle.
<color=#000000>Perhaps I must re-examine Theresa and Kal'tsit's plan.</color>

<color=#000000>Babel's research has proceeded faster than expected, but Terra's political structure is rather primitive, and Babel does not yet have the ability to transcend the barriers of race and nation so that it may represent Terra as a whole.</color>
Believe in Terra. Believe in the people to build their own future.
<color=#000000>Carry on with the project. At least the vestiges of those who came before can live on within Originium.</color>

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Well, how could I ever blame you?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I understand your dilemma. Our debates are far beyond what those little lifeforms known as humans could participate in.

spans.text: I understand your dilemma. Our debates are far beyond what those little lifeforms known as

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But this is the only way. You and I both know that much.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: If, perhaps, we still have time before Its return, we can envision things together, achieve them together. Describe anything and everything within the boundaries of the universe together.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I hope that in those fragile moments, you will always stand by my side.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: You will, won't you?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: And that concludes my report, Your Highness.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Military Commission seems to be certain we will retake region C8-10's village and supplies, but by building an outpost there, they have already fallen into a trap.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: There are, however, some officers who have begun to use tactics completely different from Manfred's. This is highly irregular.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Our spies have reported seeing Nachzehrers entering the troops' camp.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Nezzsalem...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What does the Doctor make of it?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: The Doctor believes that no matter how the Sarkaz God of War intends to participate in this conflict, our arrangements will be thrown into complete disarray.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Everyone is well aware that many members of the Royal Court have always favored the Military Commission, which advocates for reprisals and violence.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: But on account of certain restrictions—ones that you might even call rules of convention—none of them are willing to participate in the civil war.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: If the sovereigns were to decide to wage war upon us in Kazdel, those Sarkaz who have not yet returned would once more be unable to find Babel on the map.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Practically speaking, if the Court sides against us, the military gap will be concerning. Plus those that support us are, for the most part, not warriors or soldiers.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: For many of our troops, this is the first time they have ever held a weapon.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: This is why I must speak my mind. No matter how you look at the facts, our situation is changing dramatically.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Keep monitoring the Nachzehrer Court.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If Nezzsalem is no longer holding back, then Duq'arael is likely to act as well.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: For three weeks in a row, 'the Rose Riverside has no Canoes.'

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Rose Riverside is a most excellent spy network. They are able to deceive anyone they so wish, except for their sovereign lord.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Tell them to pull out immediately. Leave Kazdel if they must. Lie low in other lands.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: It will be done.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I'll take my leave then, Highness.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Royal Court. They possess the most direct capacity to use force. Nezzsalem only agreed to hand over command because he was promised a war that would reshape the land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Although rather troublesome, it is a challenge that we would have had to face sooner or later, if we were to achieve all that we hope for.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Babel does not blindly reject violence. It is clear to us all that if necessary, we must use force to defend our beliefs.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But this also means that the Sarkaz will further devour themselves, venting the hate they hold for the land by setting themselves ablaze.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It will mean the end of us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Defeating the Military Commission will not solve all our problems. We must give closure to those Sarkaz who have grown up knowing only hatred and suffering, in other regards as well.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As for Oripathy and Originium, we—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Please, enter.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Your Highness.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Your wounds have not yet fully healed, Ascalon. There is no need for you to make your report in person.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I've recovered. Besides, this is top priority. Hoederer's team has successfully intercepted a witchcraft decoder.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: The Doctor has already begun deciphering our enemy's codes. I believe we should see results soon.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Is that so...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Ines. W.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You have done very well.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Thank you, Your Highness. I hope we'll crack our enemy's comms as quickly as possible, so we can plan our next ops.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Where is your captain, by the way?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hoederer took a few flesh wounds, nothing too serious. He's getting treated in the infirmary right now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: If that is the case, then I will not waste your time. Go to him.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Of course. Thank you kindly, Highness.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: W.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Eh? What?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Go to Hoederer.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Oh. I...

steps.name: W
steps.text: Alright, got it.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Guess he still ain't dead...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: If that is all, Your Highness, I have other business—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That reminds me...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I still haven't thought of a real name for the girl, have I?
1093, Winter
Weather/Rainy
Kazdel Border, Kazdel
The Doctor listens to the pitter-patter of the rain on the leaves, eyes closed.
Drip. Drop.
The Doctor's heart rages, filled with torment. A fowlbeast cries out in the distance.
Answer my questions, or die here.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Ask away.
Are you betraying Babel?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I've never been a Babel member, but I've also never abandoned them to face their struggles alone.
Why have you come to me?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I have a request.
I will not speak to a myth with no name... evil spirit.
Who are you?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...{@nickname}. Doctor {@nickname}.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...{@nickname}.
Theresis lowers his weapon, the rain falling from the corners of his eyes onto the earth.
He does not look at the one who invited him to this clandestine meeting, instead gazing upwards at the colossal statues of so-called heroes.

spans.text: He does not look at the one who invited him to this clandestine meeting, instead gazing upwards at the colossal statues of so-called

steps.text: Statues raised to commemorate the founding of the nomadic city of Kazdel by a pair of twins.
Even after a hundred years, his stone self still stands, sword drawn, by her side, despite the best efforts of Catastrophe and storm.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Not long after she had crushed the rebellion that sought to destroy the new city, the joyful people of Kazdel invited us to witness the unveiling of these two statues.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: (Ancient Sarkaz language) Heroes.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They were to watch over the border we had marked with our own two hands for generations to come, warning our foes, welcoming our friends.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I once swore an oath to her below her statue. My sword would behead all who stand against her.
The Doctor stares at the statue of Theresis, gaze unbreaking.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Does the Military Commission not stand against her?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: No. There is no part of Kazdel that has truly risen up against her. Her foe is me, and me alone.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And what of you?
Theresis looks at the figure before him: Rainwater gathering at the hem of a long, hooded coat, rhythmically dripping onto the ground.
The shallow puddles below ripple as falling drops strike them.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You ought to remember that most Sarkaz who once lived here have long since died, lost to history. There are only a handful left who know how to find this place.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You came here on foot. How far have you walked?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Very far.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You have broken the witchcraft cipher created by Manfred's team that he's so proud of.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I did that a long time ago. I just never told anybody.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Even Theresa believes that I only began my work recently. Meaning, I'm in possession of nearly all of the Military Commission's battle plans.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: So I created this opportunity to meet you. Alone.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You are confident that I would not kill the strategist who poses the greatest threat?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I am confident that what I'm about to offer is worth enough that you wouldn't.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Technology that can control Originium.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: How far can you go under so much pressure from Victoria? How do you plan to completely change the Sarkaz, and even this entire land?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I can give you the answer you need.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You are a boastful one.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: So, what is it you wish me to do, evil spirit?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...Destroy Babel. Scatter her followers. Let Theresa in on your plans.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Unify the Sarkaz under a Kazdel ruled by the Military Commission.
The Doctor has imagined the emotions that speaking these words would incite, many times over.
'Destroy Babel'...
Only a sense of relief came over the Doctor.
The Doctor stares at the statue of Theresa, unmoving, without the slightest hint of emotion.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: She and I have never relied on the charity of our enemies, in the course of leading Kazdel to where it stands today.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It is true that this war will only end with the decisive defeat of one of us. But you should not be the one to propose it.

spans.text: It is true that this war will only end with the decisive defeat of one of us. But
should not be the one to propose it.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Proceed. Tell me more of why you would make this request, evil spirit of an age long gone.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You already know. There are no surprises here. Considering the near two hundred years you and Theresa spent working together, you should be able to guess.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I seek... the expansion of Originium.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Babel's struggles will only prolong the dying gasps of this land, Theresis.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No matter if you resist it or accept it, Originium will take on myriad forms, drawing all of civilization into her embrace.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Have you ever... looked up at the sky?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Beyond that sky, far beyond the twin moons, there is a place that we would once return to, where we would sleep peacefully.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But I am the only one left, here speaking with you. In the course of the Sarkaz's eternal search for the remains of dead gods to fend off your enemies, have you ever wondered...?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Why did those gods die?
The rain intensifies. The Doctor draws tight that trademark hood, and stands below the towering statues.
The shadows of the statues envelop the Doctor, making this figure seem ever more insignificant.
Theresis suddenly feels that the one standing before him in the rain is even harder to read than before.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The burden I bear is greater than the future of the Sarkaz. If I must destroy some things to create a ladder I hope for...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I will do it. It's all I can do.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I've already hesitated for far too long.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Destroy some things, to create a ladder...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You speak lightly of sacrifice.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Nothing light here, Theresis.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Believe me when I say, you couldn't even conceive of what I've been through.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And where do I see your sincerity for our cooperation?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Is the Shard not enough for you? Otherwise, even with the help of the Confessarii, you—

spans.text: not enough for you? Otherwise, even with the help of the Confessarii, you—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It is not. It is far from enough, evil spirit.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It is only enough to spare your life. Only enough to stop me, leader of the Military Commission, from killing a fated foe here and now.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I require an even more direct means to advance this war to the next stage.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: If you wish for the Babel members to be spared, then so be it.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Military Commission promises you that as long as Babel concedes defeat and departs Kazdel, we will not exterminate those who desert or surrender.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: But you know what you must do in return.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No... You can't...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Who would have thought that the evil spirit, who so roused the interest of the Nachzehrer King, would be such a coward?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You can't both let Theresa live and allow the Babel members to leave safely; it's a total contradiction.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Only with the destruction of Babel and the complete eradication of its members can Theresa leave for Londinium with me.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Otherwise, it would merely be a case of the Military Commission quashing and dispersing yet another group of civilians, migrants, and pacifists.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Even without my order, such things will happen naturally.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Perhaps you believe that Theresa would be willing to step back and watch it before her eyes? She will not. And so she will resist.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You know what I ask of you. If you truly wish to save the many who stand by your side, make them willingly admit defeat and surrender to me...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Then slay their king.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And then, I will allow Babel to leave. As it collapses, it will no longer be considered a Sarkaz endeavor, and it will grow weak, drifting to the edges of civilization.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: 'Destroy some things to create a ladder', {@nickname}.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You're right. There is nothing light about this.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: In your opinion, what is the meaning behind this civil war? What meaning would her death hold?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Reclaiming our lands, rebuilding our homes, ending discrimination, and revitalizing our race. You will have heard these platitudes many times.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They are too complex, and yet too simple.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Merely a small and pitiful species trying to grasp their fate.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: In that case, I will tip the scales of destiny.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Destroy Babel, divide them, weaken them. Allow them to return to their former lives, so that they can know a moment of peace in the final century.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: That way... we don't have to kill Theresa. Or at the very least, we can minimize the loss of life.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Fretting over violence serves only to stifle you. You understand the Sarkaz better than most, but perhaps still not well enough.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I have a question myself, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Evil spirit of a bygone age, you who call yourself a giant, a god, a supreme creator, one who can dictate the fate of the Sarkaz. Are you the only one of your kind?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...I am.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: That is good to know. Go, now, without guilt, and do what you have decided to do.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: If you worry there will be no one to tear you down from your lofty heights, or judge your sins. Don't. I will do it, evil spirit.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Until there are none left to toy with our fate.
The Doctor listens to the splashing of the puddles behind, the sound of footsteps fading into the distance.
Theresis is gone, wishing to stay not a moment longer.
Pale sunlight begins to seep through the gaps between the statues.
The Doctor cannot feel the slightest bit of warmth from it.
The heroes continue to gaze into the distance. They do not look beneath their feet.
There stands a figure who does not leave for a long, long time.
